L1-A1.scenario: Neralis Meltworks is checking 24 fictitious EAF heats from its Kestrel plant. The superintendent needs total output, average tap time and one pooled metal-yield result. Every mass is in metric tonnes; each row is one heat.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the total tapped mass for all 24 heats, in metric tonnes.
Calculate the average tap duration for all 24 heats, in minutes. Submit the unrounded numeric value.
Calculate pooled metal yield as 100 times total tapped mass divided by total charged mass. Submit the unrounded percentage number, for example 93.4 rather than 0.934.
Calculate the difference between average charged mass and average tapped mass, in tonnes. Submit an unrounded number.
Calculate aggregate tapped tonnes per hour using total tap duration, rather than averaging individual heat rates.

L1-A2.scenario: Velora Office Supply is reconciling 26 fictitious customer orders. Every order has a text order code, a shipment reference, a units count and a value in Canadian dollars. A complete order register should count records without mistaking text codes for numbers.

tasks.prompt: Count numeric entries in the Units column. Do not total the units.
Count populated Order_code cells, excluding the heading.
Count numeric entries in Order_code. The task concerns the stored cell type, not the digits inside each text code.
Calculate value per recorded order: total Order_value_CAD divided by the count of populated Order_code cells. Submit the unrounded number.
Calculate average units per recorded shipment using total units and the count of Shipment_ref entries.

L1-A3.scenario: Orvanta Tube Lab is reviewing 28 fictitious tensile specimens from the Talren rolling line. Yield strength and tensile strength are measured in MPa; elongation is a percentage. The report needs observed extremes and spread, without declaring compliance with any real specification.

tasks.prompt: Find the lowest Yield_MPa across all specimens.
Find the highest Tensile_MPa across all specimens.
Calculate the observed elongation range: largest minus smallest Elongation_pct, in percentage points.
Calculate maximum tensile strength divided by minimum yield strength. Submit the unrounded dimensionless ratio.
Calculate 100 times the yield-strength range divided by mean yield strength. Submit the unrounded percentage number.

L1-A4.scenario: Ruvella Parts Depot is planning stock for 30 fictitious items. Demand is in units, while replenishment uses complete packs; stock can contain a partial pack. Unit costs include extra decimal places so the invoice policy can round each line to cents.

tasks.prompt: Round the first item’s Unit_cost_CAD to two decimal places.
For the first five items, calculate the number of complete packs to order to meet Demand_units. Return one integer per row in dataset order.
For the first five items, calculate complete packs contained in Stock_units. Ignore any incomplete remainder. Return integers in dataset order.
For the first five items, calculate Stock_units times Unit_cost_CAD, rounding each item value to two decimal places. Return values in dataset order.
Total the five individually rounded stock values from task 4. Round that total to two decimal places.

L1-A5.scenario: Kesvani Gauge Works is checking 32 fictitious pipe-wall samples against a training-only target of 12.70 mm with tolerance ±0.20 mm. These values are not a real product standard. The workbook stores target in Parameters!B2 and tolerance in Parameters!B3; keep those cells fixed when copying.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the absolute distance of the first sample’s Measured_mm from the fixed target, in mm. Reference Parameters!B2.
Calculate the absolute distance between mean Measured_mm for all 32 samples and the fixed target. Submit the unrounded value in mm.

Classify the first eight samples as Pass when their distance from target is at most the tolerance; otherwise Hold. Return exact labels in dataset order. Reference the fixed Parameters cells. Round each deviation to two decimal places before comparing, matching the measurement precision.

Return Release if the minimum measured thickness is at least target minus tolerance AND the maximum is at most target plus tolerance. Otherwise return Hold. Use nested decisions or another valid approach; evaluate all 32 samples.
Return Centred if mean thickness is within 0.05 mm of target, inclusive; otherwise Investigate. Reference Parameters!B2.

L2-A1.scenario: Novrila Procurement is screening 22 fictitious suppliers. An order can proceed only with approval, no credit hold, lead time at most 10 days and quality score at least 95%. Separate alerts explain why a supplier needs review.

tasks.prompt: For the first supplier, return Eligible when Lead_days is at most 10 and Quality_score_pct is at least 95; otherwise Review. Ignore approval and credit status for this task.
For the first eight suppliers, return Alert if Lead_days exceeds 10 OR Quality_score_pct is below 95. Otherwise return Clear. Keep dataset order.
For the first eight suppliers, return Allowed when Credit_hold is not Yes, otherwise Blocked. Keep dataset order and use a logical reversal.

For the first eight suppliers, return Order only when Approved is Yes, Credit_hold is not Yes, Lead_days is at most 10 and Quality_score_pct is at least 95. Otherwise return Do not order. Keep dataset order.
For the first supplier, return Escalate if it is approved but either has a credit hold or fails the lead-time/quality screen. Otherwise return Routine.

L2-A2.scenario: Pelvaris Mill is triaging 24 fictitious downtime events. Some events lose zero units, which is a valid measurement rather than missing data. Supervisors need duration bands and cost-per-lost-unit decisions that explain zero-denominator cases.

tasks.prompt: Classify the first event’s Duration_min as Short for at most 10 minutes, Medium for more than 10 through 30 minutes, or Long for more than 30 minutes.
For the first six events, calculate Labor_cost_CAD per Units_lost, rounded to two decimals. Return No lost units when the ratio is undefined. Keep dataset order.
For the first six events, classify Duration_min as Critical for at least 45 minutes, Priority for at least 20 but less than 45, otherwise Routine. Keep dataset order.
For the first eight events, return Review when the unrounded Labor_cost_CAD per Units_lost exceeds 15, otherwise Accept. Return No loss when the ratio is undefined. Keep dataset order.
Calculate overall labour cost per lost unit across all 24 events, rounded to two decimals. Include labour cost from zero-loss events in the total cost.

L2-A3.scenario: Averiq Stationery is reviewing 26 fictitious September sales lines. The commercial team needs results for a region, channel and product category together. Revenue already represents the whole sales line, so it must not be multiplied by units again.

tasks.prompt: Total Revenue_CAD for Region Cove, including both channels and both categories.
Count sales lines that are both Region Cove and Channel Wholesale. Count rows rather than sold units.
Total Revenue_CAD for Region Cove, Channel Wholesale and Category Supplies together.
Calculate revenue per sales line for Region Cove and Channel Wholesale, rounded to two decimals. Divide that group’s total revenue by its matching line count. Use No sales if no matching rows exist.
Total Revenue_CAD for Region Cove lines with Revenue_CAD at least 500, including the 500 boundary.

L2-A4.scenario: Tervalon Pipe Services is examining 28 fictitious repair records. The team wants typical repair time for selected cells and shifts, plus cost attributed to one defect family. A training-only prioritization rule combines a group average with total Seam-repair cost.

tasks.prompt: Calculate unrounded mean Repair_min for Cell Mill-2, across all shifts and defect families.
Calculate mean Repair_cost_CAD for Cell Mill-2, Shift Night and Defect_family Seam, rounded to two decimals. Use No repairs if the group has no numeric observations.
Total Repair_cost_CAD for Defect_family Seam, across both cells and shifts.
Return Prioritize if mean Repair_min for Mill-2 Night records exceeds 40 AND total Repair_cost_CAD for all Seam records exceeds 1500. Otherwise return Monitor. These are separate groups, as stated.
Calculate the percentage of total repair cost attributed to Seam records, rounded to two decimals. Submit a percentage number, not a fraction.

L2-A5.scenario: Solvani Distribution is reviewing 30 fictitious shipment records. Delivered and In transit records must not be mixed when judging observed lead times. One invented carrier has no delivered shipments, so the report must distinguish an absent group from a genuine zero-day result.

tasks.prompt: Find the longest Lead_days for Carrier Zephra with Status Delivered, across both regions.
Find the shortest Lead_days for Carrier Zephra, Region North and Status Delivered together.
Calculate longest minus shortest Lead_days for Zephra North Delivered shipments. Use the same three-condition group for both extremes.
For Carrier Vanta with Status Delivered, return its longest Lead_days if at least one matching row exists; otherwise return No matching shipments. Do not use zero as the absence label.
Return Met when at least one Zephra North Delivered record exists and its longest Lead_days is at most 5. Otherwise return Review.

L3-A1.scenario: Arelvon Tube Lab has 24 invented tensile samples. Match each Product_code to the Specs sheet; a blank or unlisted code must return Missing, and repeated sample records remain separate. These limits are fictitious training rules, not a published standard.

tasks.prompt: Look up Yield_min_MPa for the first sample’s Product_code.
Return the second Specs row’s Yield_min_MPa by its position within the four-row specification array.
For the first six samples, return Pass if Yield_MPa is at least the matched minimum, Hold if below it, or Missing if the product key is blank/unlisted. Keep dataset order.
For the first sample, calculate Yield_MPa divided by its matched minimum, rounded to three decimals.
Return the final specification row’s Product_code using its array position.

L3-A2.scenario: Belvori Services has 26 invented employee expense records and six allowance codes. Duplicate employee names are legitimate; Employee_code identifies the record. One unknown and one blank Band_code must receive Missing.

tasks.prompt: Find the 1-based position of the first employee’s Band_code within Allowances!A2:A7.
Return the third allowance amount using its row position.
For the first six employees, retrieve Monthly_allowance_CAD by exact Band_code, returning Missing for unknown or blank bands.
For the first employee, calculate Claim_CAD minus its matched allowance, rounded to two decimals.
For the first employee, return Review when Claim_CAD exceeds the matched allowance, otherwise Within.

L3-A3.scenario: Corvani Alloy Lab has 28 invented inspection records. Each required energy depends on both Grade_code and Orientation, using the Matrix sheet. A blank grade and an unknown orientation are included so an incomplete lookup cannot silently select a default.

tasks.prompt: Find the first record’s Grade_code position in Matrix!A2:A5.
Find the first record’s Orientation position within Matrix!B1:C1.
For the first six records, return their energy requirement in J from the two-dimensional matrix, or Missing for an absent grade/orientation.
For the first record, return Pass if Energy_J meets or exceeds its two-way requirement, otherwise Hold.
Return the difference between the first grade’s LPA and TWA requirements: LPA minus TWA.

L3-A4.scenario: Delvori Logistics is pricing 30 invented shipments using ascending lower-bound mass bands. Each band includes its lower bound and continues up to the next bound; duplicate masses are valid observations. A negative mass is invalid and must not match a price band.

tasks.prompt: Return Rate_CAD_per_km for the first shipment’s mass using the stated lower-bound bands.
Return the first mass’s 1-based band position within Bands!A2:A5.
For the first six shipments, return the rate for each nonnegative mass and Invalid for negative mass.
For the first shipment, calculate Distance_km times the matched rate, rounded to cents.
Return Rate_CAD_per_km for a hypothetical 99.9 kg shipment.

L3-A5.scenario: Esvani Inspection receives 32 invented sample records and a Limits table. A repeated product key in Limits is deliberately ambiguous; blank/unlisted keys are also present. Use a requirement only when exactly one matching specification row exists.

tasks.prompt: For the first six inspection rows, count matching Product_code entries in Limits, excluding its header.
Return the first unique product’s hardness limit using INDEX/MATCH.
For the first six rows, return the hardness limit only when exactly one Limits row matches; otherwise return Review key.
For the first six rows, return Pass for hardness at most a unique limit, Hold above it, or Review key for any ambiguous/absent key.
Count Limits rows with product EX-2.

L4-A1.scenario: Felnori Mill has 44 invented imported inspection IDs. ASCII tab characters, ordinary outer spaces and inconsistent letter case are deliberate; no nonbreaking spaces occur. Repeated canonical IDs are legitimate retests and must remain separate records.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, remove ASCII control characters, trim ordinary spaces and return uppercase canonical inspection IDs.
Remove control characters and outer ordinary spaces from the first raw ID, preserving its original letter case.
For the first six records, return Retest when the canonical uppercase ID is FN-101, otherwise Other.
Count populated raw inspection ID cells across all 44 rows. Retests still count as records.
Return the first cleaned uppercase ID followed by the literal text |CHECK.

L4-A2.scenario: Gorvella Inventory has 48 invented item codes in the fixed pattern AA-NNN-Z. Outer ordinary spaces and mixed-case prefixes are present. Each row is an inventory observation, including repeats of the same SKU.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, return the two-letter uppercase prefix after trimming.
For the first six records, return the three-character numeric segment as text, preserving leading zeros.
For the first six records, return the final one-letter suffix.
For the first six records, return Priority for suffix A, otherwise Standard.
Calculate first-row stock value, rounded to cents.

L4-A3.scenario: Hervani Testworks has 52 invented key strings HEAT|SAMPLE|ORIENTATION. Mixed orientation case and ordinary spaces are present; two malformed records lack delimiters. Return Missing for a malformed key rather than guessing its components.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, return the heat segment before the first |, trimmed; return Missing when no delimiter exists.
For the first six records, return the orientation after the last |, trimmed and uppercase; preserve the mixed-case fallback Missing.
For the first six records, return the sample segment between the two delimiters; return Missing for malformed keys.
For the first six records, return Transverse when the normalized final orientation is TWA, Longitudinal for LPA, or Missing for a malformed key.
Return the first row’s heat segment plus / plus sample segment.

L4-A4.scenario: Irvella Dispatch has 56 invented manifests in the three-field pattern ORDER|ZONE|PRIORITY. Some Zone fields are intentionally empty; their field positions must be preserved. Blank zones receive Unknown in the standardized display.

tasks.prompt: Split the first manifest into three columns: order, zone and priority. Preserve the empty zone as an empty cell.
For the second manifest, return a readable summary joined with the exact delimiter space / space, ignoring empty fields.
For the first six manifests, return their middle zone; replace an empty zone with Unknown.
For the first manifest, rebuild all three fields using delimiter | and keeping empty fields; the result must equal the source.
Return the first manifest’s priority in uppercase.

L4-A5.scenario: Jelvani Quality Services has 60 invented readings for a training report. Raw sample IDs use underscores and inconsistent case; numeric measurements must remain numeric in Data. Messages need stable decimal places and standardized text.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, replace all underscores with hyphens, trim ordinary spaces and uppercase the sample ID.
For the first six records, return Reading_mm as text with exactly three decimals.
For the first six technicians, return title-case names.

For the first six records, create messages SAMPLE: 0.00 mm | STATUS, where SAMPLE is the normalized ID, STATUS is Review if the unrounded reading exceeds 13.00, otherwise Within. Use exactly the shown spaces and two displayed decimals.
Return the first reading rounded numerically to two decimals.

L5-A1.scenario: Kelvani Materials Lab has 44 invented test-date components. Dates are valid numeric year/month/day values, avoiding locale-dependent parsing. Reporting months use calendar month ends; repeated test dates remain separate samples.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, construct dates and return ISO text yyyy-mm-dd.
For the first six records, return the calendar month-end cutoff as ISO text.
For the first record, count calendar days from its test date to month end, excluding the starting date.
Count all records whose Month component equals 7.
Return the month end three calendar months after the first test date, as ISO text.

L5-A2.scenario: Lervella Stores has 48 invented replenishment records. Year, month and day are explicit components; first-row January 31 exercises a shorter-month boundary. Renewal_months are whole calendar months, not fixed 30-day intervals.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, return the renewal date after Renewal_months calendar months, as ISO text.
For the first six records, return the month end of each renewal month as ISO text.
For the first record, calculate elapsed calendar days from the starting date to its renewal date.
Calculate first-row order value rounded to cents.
Return the first record’s month end one month before its starting date, as ISO text.

L5-A3.scenario: Melvani Process Lab has 52 invented review starts and target working-day durations. Only the two dates in Holidays are excluded; they are invented shutdown days, not a statutory holiday calendar. Saturday and Sunday are weekends.

tasks.prompt: First create Holidays!E2:E3 as real dates using the Year/Month/Day components in B:D. Then return those two dates as ISO text in their source order.
For the first six reviews, return the deadline Target_workdays working days after the start date, excluding the stated shutdown dates. Submit ISO text.
For the first six reviews, count working days inclusively from the start date through the computed deadline, excluding the stated shutdowns.
For the first six reviews, return Extended when the inclusive working-day count exceeds 6, otherwise Standard.
Return the first review’s deadline with no shutdown exclusions, as ISO text.

L5-A4.scenario: Norvella Business Support has 56 invented employment records. Use the fixed reporting date October 1, 2026, not today. Dates are provided as explicit components; completed years/months exclude partial intervals.

tasks.prompt: For the first six employees, return completed years of service through October 1, 2026.
For the first six employees, return completed months of service through the same fixed date.
For the first six start dates, return Monday-start calendar week numbers under WEEKNUM return type 2.
For the first six employees, return Established for at least three completed years, otherwise Developing.
Count employees with Year component 2025 across the entire register.

L5-A5.scenario: Orvani Rolling has 60 invented shifts with start/end hour and minute components. Every shift lasts under 24 hours; a lower end time means it crosses midnight. Unpaid break minutes are subtracted once, and training Review means net hours strictly above 8.

tasks.prompt: For the first six shifts, return the start time as text hh:mm.
For the first six shifts, calculate gross hours across midnight, rounded to two decimals.
For the first six shifts, calculate net hours after subtracting Break_min once, rounded to two decimals.
For the first six shifts, return Review if unrounded net hours strictly exceed 8, otherwise Standard.
Return the first shift’s gross duration in minutes as an unrounded number.

L6-A1.scenario: Pervani Tube Inspection has 64 invented length measurements. Blank Length_mm means not measured and must be excluded from threshold analysis; zero is not used as a substitute. Review rows are measured lengths strictly below 5985 mm.

tasks.prompt: Return all Inspection_code values for measured Length_mm below 5985, preserving source order.
Return all measured Length_mm below 5985 sorted ascending, preserving duplicate observations.
Count the measured rows below 5985 across the whole dataset.
Return Inspection_code and Length_mm as two columns for Tovrin rows with measured Length_mm below 5985, in source order.
Return None when filtering inspection codes for the nonexistent line Absent.

L6-A2.scenario: Qervella Orders has 68 invented orders with Urgency_score and Order_value_CAD. Scores and values can repeat; Order_code ascending is the final tie-break. Blank Customer_code fields are intentional and do not remove an order from the queue.

tasks.prompt: Return all Order_code values sorted by Urgency_score descending, Order_value_CAD descending, then Order_code ascending.
Return the first and last source Order_code values as a two-row column.
Return the first three complete queue records (four columns) under the stated three-key ordering.
For the first six source records, return High when Urgency_score is at least 4, otherwise Normal.
Return the third record’s Order_code in the sorted queue.

L6-A3.scenario: Relvani Melt Tracking has 72 invented sample records spanning six heat codes. Heat codes repeat across samples; one blank code represents an incomplete record and must be excluded from the distinct register. Sample counts must still reflect all valid records per heat.

tasks.prompt: Return distinct nonblank Heat_no values sorted ascending.
Return display numbers 1 through 6 as a six-row column.
Return the sample-record counts for the six sorted nonblank heats in the same order as the register.
Return two columns: sorted nonblank Heat_no and its record count.
Count records with a blank Heat_no.

L6-A4.scenario: Servella Stock Control has 40 invented warehouse-A observations and 40 separate warehouse-B observations on Secondary. Schemas and units are aligned; repeated SKU values across warehouses remain separate records. One blank SKU in each extract must not be included in the ranked report.

tasks.prompt: Return the first three Data records followed by the first three Secondary records, as six rows and four columns.
For the first five Data records, return two columns: SKU and Stock_units, aligned in source order.
Return the first five records of the full combined raw extract (Data followed by Secondary), including all four columns.
Return the first three combined raw records after removing the first two records, as three rows and four columns.
Return the highest-stock valid record as four columns. Exclude blank SKUs; sort stock descending, SKU ascending, then Warehouse ascending to break ties.

L6-A5.scenario: Tervani Charpy Lab has 80 invented records: 40 sample/heat pairs, each with LPA and TWA orientations. Sample_no repeats across four heats, so both keys are essential; orientation case/spaces vary and one TWA energy is blank. Missing energy must be reported as Missing, never zero.

tasks.prompt: Return the 40 distinct Sample_no and Heat_no row pairs as two columns, in first-occurrence order. Use the exact output B2:C41 as the helper register for later tasks.
Return the first and last source records, all four columns, as a two-row array.
Using the helper register B2:C41, return two columns: LPA energy and TWA energy for each pair, in helper order. Trim/uppercase orientations and return Missing for an absent or blank energy.
Return the complete 40-row report with four columns: Sample_no, Heat_no, LPA energy, TWA energy. Use the helper register and the two orientation columns from Task 3; keep helper order.
For sample 1 in heat TH-7401, return Review if its TWA energy is missing, otherwise Measured.

EX-A1.scenario: Ravellen Tube Works has 60 fictitious pipe inspections. Normalize Grade_code, match a unique Specs key and apply the invented minimum yield strength. Blank strength or an unknown grade means Review. Equality meets the training rule. Rework cost is Length_m × Unit_cost_CAD rounded per pipe to two decimals. These limits are training assumptions, not a published standard or production acceptance decision.

tasks.prompt: Normalize every Grade_code with ordinary-space trimming and uppercase. Keep Data order.
For every pipe, return Released, Rework or Review under the scenario rules. Keep Data order. Do not treat a blank strength as zero.
Return only Rework pipes in two columns: Pipe_no and rounded rework cost (CAD). Sort cost descending, then Pipe_no ascending. Paste all 27 rows, without headers.
Return one row: Released count, Rework count, Review count, total rounded rework cost (CAD). Use all 60 records and round the final cost to two decimals.
Return the average measured Yield_MPa for Released pipes, rounded to two decimals.

EX-A2.scenario: Chelloran Test Lab has 80 fictitious observations: twenty sample/heat pairs, two orientations and two replicate slots per orientation. Sample_no alone is not unique. Group by BOTH Sample_no and Heat_no. Normalize Orientation using TRIM/UPPER. Average numeric replicate energies (J), include measured zero, ignore blanks, round to two decimals and return Missing when no numeric observation exists. Do not select the first duplicate measurement.

tasks.prompt: Normalize all 80 Orientation labels using ordinary-space trimming and uppercase. Preserve Data order.
Return the twenty distinct Sample_no and Heat_no pairs, sorted Sample_no ascending, then Heat_no ascending. Preserve the three-character sample identifiers.
For the sorted pairs, return two columns: mean LPA energy and mean TWA energy (J). Apply the numeric-replicate and Missing rules. Keep the key order from Task 2.
Return the final twenty-row report: Sample_no, Heat_no, mean LPA_J, mean TWA_J. Preserve the Task 2 sort order and Missing labels.
Count sample/heat pairs missing at least one orientation mean. Count each pair once.

EX-A3.scenario: Ildavon Supply records 60 fictitious inventory movements. Stock provides six unique SKUs, opening units and minimum units. Normalize Movement with TRIM/UPPER. Receipt adds units; Dispatch and Scrap subtract units. All SKUs are valid and quantities are nonnegative. Negative closing stock is meaningful and must remain visible. Reorder when closing units are strictly below the minimum; equality does not reorder.

tasks.prompt: Return signed units for every movement. Receipt is positive; Dispatch and Scrap are negative. Keep Data order.

For all six SKUs in Stock order, return six columns: SKU, opening units, receipt units, dispatch units, scrap units, closing units. Movement totals are positive; closing = opening + receipts - dispatch - scrap.
Return the 2 SKUs needing reorder in three columns: SKU, closing units, shortage to minimum. Sort closing ascending, then SKU ascending. Preserve negative closing values.

Return one row: source net movement units, source opening units, dashboard closing units, reconciliation difference (dashboard closing - source opening - source net movement). Recompute source net directly from Data rather than summing the Task 1 helper.
Calculate the quantity-weighted Unit_cost_CAD for Dispatch movements only, rounded to four decimals. Use dispatched units as the denominator.
